name: Gonial angle reduction (V-line surgery)

card.summary: Surgical shaving of the lower jaw angle (and sometimes chin) to narrow the lower face; established in East Asian aesthetic surgery, evidence is mostly surgeon case series.
card.aka: V-line surgery, mandible angle reduction, mandibular contouring
card.note: Major elective jaw surgery; the evidence base is largely surgeon-reported series rather than controlled trials.

quick.overview:
Gonial angle reduction removes bone from the corner of the lower jaw (the gonial angle) so that the face looks narrower and tapers toward the chin, the so-called V-line. It is often combined with chin reshaping (genioplasty) and is discussed in the aesthetic surgery literature mainly in the context of East Asian patients with wide lower faces.

In looksmaxxing forums it sits at the opposite end from jaw implants: instead of adding width and angularity, it removes them. Published evidence consists mainly of surgeon case descriptions and technique papers; no randomized trials were found.
quick.mechanism: Through incisions inside the mouth, the surgeon resects a portion of the mandibular angle, and in some designs also the outer cortex of the lower border, and may reshape the chin. A 1991 paper classified patients into types by the degree of angle protrusion and matched the amount of resection to each type. Botulinum toxin in the masseter muscle is a non-surgical alternative that some papers describe for slimming the lower face.
quick.risks: Reported risks of mandibular contouring in the literature include nerve injury, bleeding, infection, asymmetry and unsatisfactory contour; the Wikipedia article on facial feminization surgery names damage to the mental nerve as the greatest risk of jaw and chin reshaping. It is performed under general anesthesia and has a recovery period with swelling.

lead: Gonial angle reduction, commonly marketed as V-line surgery, is a cosmetic jaw-contouring operation in which bone is removed from the angle of the mandible, where the lower border of the jaw meets the vertical ramus, in order to narrow the lower face and give it a tapered, V-shaped outline. It is frequently paired with reshaping of the chin.[1][2]

The surgical literature on aesthetic mandibular contouring dates at least to a 1991 paper describing angle reduction and genioplasty for purely aesthetic reasons, which graded patients by the degree of angle protrusion.[2] The topic appears in later work on Asian patients seeking a slimmer lower face, as well as in facial feminization surgery, where jaw reduction is one of several procedures used to soften a masculine lower face.[3][4][5]

The evidence base consists mostly of technique descriptions and surgeon-reported case series; no randomized controlled trials were found. Reviews of the area note that surgical angle reduction is a complex procedure with significant risks and downtime, which has led some surgeons to describe less invasive options such as botulinum toxin injection into the masseter muscles.[6][7]
infobox: Gonial angle and lower border of the mandible; often chin

paras: The gonial angle is the corner of the mandible at the back of the jawline. A prominent or wide angle can make the lower face look broad or square when viewed from the front. In angle reduction, a surgeon removes part of this region through the mouth, so the outline of the jaw appears narrower.[2][6]

The 1991 classification divided patients into types A, B and C according to how far the angle protrudes. In the mildest, an angle resection alone was described; more prominent angles required additional resection of the lower border or combination with other procedures.[2] The same paper presented genioplasty, reshaping of the chin, as the second main operation used for contour change without orthodontic treatment.[2]

A related procedure, sometimes called a mini V-line, narrows the chin itself and has been described as important for achieving a feminine lower face.[8] Sliding genioplasty techniques are also used in facial feminization surgery.[9]

sections.h: Use in facial feminization and Asian aesthetic surgery
paras: Facial feminization surgery is a group of procedures intended to change male facial features toward female ones, and is performed mainly for transgender women with gender dysphoria, although some non-transgender women also seek parts of it.[10] Reviews of gender-affirming surgery list jaw and chin contouring among the procedures used.[11] The Wikipedia article on the subject says reducing the jaw can be done through the mouth and that shaving the masseter muscle can also narrow the jaw's appearance.[12]

A 2020 review describes mandible contouring for aesthetic enhancement in Asian patients, a population in which narrow, tapered lower faces are frequently requested.[7] A 2016 paper on patients with wide, short faces describes combining chin fat grafting with masseter botulinum toxin as an alternative to invasive angle reduction and genioplasty, which it characterizes as complex procedures with significant risks and downtime.[6]

Wikipedia's article on facial feminization surgery names damage to the mental nerve, which supplies sensation to the chin and lower lip, as the greatest risk of jaw and chin reshaping, and lists tooth-root injury, infection, bone non-union and injury to the mentalis muscle as further risks.[12]

The aesthetic mandibular contouring literature also treats asymmetry and unsatisfactory contour as outcomes the surgeon must plan against, and describes the operations as involving downtime and risk compared with injectable approaches.[6]

Published human data are limited to descriptive technique papers and surgeon case series, such as the 1991 aesthetic mandible contouring report and later reviews in Asian and feminization patients.[2][7][10] No randomized trial of gonial angle reduction for appearance was found. Registered trials that turn up in searches for the term concern unrelated topics such as mandibular fracture plates.[13]

In looksmaxxing forums, discussion of the jaw mostly concerns making it wider, longer and more angular through implants, orthognathic surgery or masseter growth; angle reduction is generally raised in the context of the opposite goal, a narrower or more tapered lower face, and of the contrast between East Asian and Western ideals of jaw shape. Some forum posters describe an ideal jaw in which the widest part of the mandible sits at the gonial angle and tapers into a defined chin, which is the shape V-line surgery aims to produce in a wider jaw.[14]

timeline.event: Facial feminization surgery begins in the US, later including jaw and chin procedures.[12]
A paper on mandibular contouring for purely aesthetic reasons classifies angle reduction by degree of protrusion.[2]
A report describes narrowing the chin by a mini V-line surgery for a feminine lower face.[8]
A paper describes chin fat grafting plus masseter botulinum toxin as an alternative to angle reduction.[6]
Review of mandible contouring for aesthetic enhancement in Asian patients.[7]

lore.intro: On looksmaxxing forums the jaw is usually discussed as something to enlarge, and V-line surgery appears as the reverse option, tied to ideals of a narrow, tapered lower face.[14]

claims.claim: A narrower, V-tapered jaw is the more attractive lower-face shape
claims.believers: Some forum posters describe a long mandible whose widest point is the gonial angle and which tapers to a sharp chin as photogenic, and say very round or wide jaws look less aesthetic.[14]
claims.experts: Surgical papers describe tapered lower faces as a frequent goal among Asian patients and feminization patients, but these are statements about patient preference rather than measured attractiveness outcomes.[6][7]

claims.claim: Botulinum toxin in the masseter can give a similar slimming effect without surgery
claims.believers: Practitioners in the aesthetic literature describe masseter injections as a popular non-invasive way to slim the lower face.[6]
claims.experts: A 2016 paper describes combining masseter toxin with chin fat grafting for wide, short faces and reports it as a minimally invasive alternative to angle reduction, but this is a technique report rather than a controlled comparison.[6]
